Geocaching is like a real world treasure hunt. You get an app on your phone, there is spin offs but there are two official ones, a free and paid one, the free will do you fine as a beginner.

The app will show you geocaches near by you, there's many caches of different difficulty etc and once you choose one, you click begin and it will give you a map on your phone, you follow it to the location, then dig around the location to try and find the cache. There may be a clue such as "Down low" and you will know then it's on the ground somewhere, under a log etc.

Once you find the cache, you open it up, sign the visitors log with your username, and you can put a trinket inside and take one that someone else has put in! (A toy soldier or something, anything you feel like, or even nothing if you'd prefer.) You can then click, Found it! on your app, and It will be logged on your profile and the geocache that you found it, and you can leave a review etc.

You can read all about it here

Searching geocaching in the app store should yield the free app to download and try, have fun.

Watching and following sports. You probably have internet/cable/tv and if not you can always go to a local sports bar.

  1. Find a team you like. Preferably a hometeam or a team from somewhere you actually have ties to not only because you don't wanna be a band-wagoner but its easier to emotionally invest in them.

  2. Follow your team. What they're doing in the preseason, regular season, and postseason. Get to know the players and what makes your team good or bad and which teams are going to be problematic for yours.

  3. Get to know your rivals. Rivalries are one of the most fantastic parts of watching sports. As a Cowboys fan watching my team beat the Reds by 40 is like getting high but watching the Eagles stomp us on Thanksgiving is crushing. Its part of the rush of being a fan.

  4. Fucking watch. Its easier than ever these days. Google your teams schedule and make commitments to watch them play (with basketball or baseball its best to pick the games with the best matchups because few people have time to watch 100+ games of one team). Watch your rivals. Watch your favorite underdog teams. Just watch. Enjoy the thrill of a close win and the sadness of a bad loss. Take in the drama. Talk shit to your friends.

People knock sports a lot but it can be a fairly cheap hobby and can keep you occupied and give you reasons to have get togethers. A lot of the joy of sports comes from emotionally investing in a team that you love. The wins and losses are that much more important to you. It can be frustrating and it can give you some serious emotional highs. During football season a win makes the following week that much better and a loss makes everything gloomy. Its also a great way to make small talk with people. Above all sports are just fun distractions that you will get out of as much as you put in.

Growing houseplants. Buy a lemon, do whatever you want with it, but save the seeds. Wash them off, this is the tricky part, don't wash them down the drain. Next take a nail file and rough then up a bit, this is supposed to help them germinate. You can put them directly into soil and hope for the best, or you can fold them up in a damp paper towel and then place that into a zip lock bag, but don't seal it, they'll need air. Be patient. It can take between 2 and 4 weeks for them to sprout, then you can pick the strongest of them and plant them in a small pot. Mine got big enough that they are now happily living in a coffee can. I have three going and I have plans (that I'm not entirely sure will work honestly) to braid the three together as they grow. If it works, it should look really nice. But you're out maybe $.33 for a lemon, $1 or so for a 2 liter bottle to cut the bottom off of for the first pot to plant it in, and $2 for a small bag of potting soil.
